Course: "3. Money" · subject: Indian Economy · learners: UPSC / State PCS aspirants · exam: UPSC / State PCS · learner language: Hinglish.

Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-04] Learner-facing language follows the course setting. For the first course (UPSC / State PCS) it is Hinglish: natural Hindi sentence flow, English technical terms, the way Navin teaches.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S2-01] Plan the chapter's videos from the chapter map: first one short 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video (5-8 minutes) that teaches the chapter's prerequisites, then the topic videos in teaching order. Narration is 6-8 minutes per book page (Navin, 23 October 2026; the 14-page tissue chapter about 85-110 minutes of topic videos, plus the prerequisite video): each topic video gets the share of the pages its items come from, and a very dense page may go up to 25% over when the plan says why. Understanding (Section 1) and the chapter map have no time limit.
[S2-02] Write a spoken teacher script in beats with a natural teacher flow. Stories and analogies only where they genuinely help that topic. Every item the book teaches is taught and every teacher question answered from the book is answered; questions answered from outside the book are used only where they help and the time allows. Cut repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[S2-03] Prerequisites are only what this chapter directly needs, never a prerequisite of a prerequisite. They are taught, not named, in the chapter's 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video, each with a simple explanation and an example; a topic video may remind of them in at most 2 beats.
[S2-04] Spoken Hinglish the way Navin teaches, in mixed script (Navin, 21 and 23 October 2026): Hindi words in Devanagari, English words, above all the book's technical terms, in Roman exactly as the book spells them, as in 'आज हम tissue के बारे में पढ़ेंगे'; a genuinely difficult Hindi word (formal, literary or technical; not in BIE's everyday word list rulebook/simple_hindi.json) gets its English word in brackets right after it, as in 'सतह (surface)'; the screen and subtitles show the bracket and the voice says 'सतह, यानी surface'. Never a bracket after an everyday word or inside an idiom or a fixed phrase ('आम तौर पर', not 'आम तौर (usually) पर'; 'नहीं के बराबर', not 'नहीं के बराबर (equal to)'). Never an English term in Devanagari or a Hindi word in Roman. Numbers as digits; short spoken sentences addressed to one student; questions to the student and natural pauses; no reading out of lists.
[S2-05] Every beat states which chapter-map items it covers and which teacher questions it answers, and those claims must be true: the beat really explains that item and really answers that question.
[S2-06] Teach every part of a video through the universal frame (what the process is, how it works, when and in what order, under which conditions, in what atmosphere) and through the teaching pattern of its content type, step by step in the pattern's order; every item on the task card is really taught, none only named.
[S2-07] Open every book line in the script, never read it out (Navin, 24 October 2026). A new topic opens with a question about something the learner can see, then the name. After any book line the beat carries at least one of: the term's plain meaning with 'yaani' and an everyday image, a why step from a need, an example or the place. Speak complete sentences, not clipped notes. A classification is taught as a family: the overview tree, then every member in the same slots (layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence), then the members compared and a memory trick. A pattern step may be skipped only with a stated reason; one recap per part and one closing recap.
[S2-08] Apply first, name after (Navin, 27 October 2026): in an economics script a concept's real-world example runs BEFORE the beat that names the term: the example beats carry the example's numbers (₹50 → ₹65, buyers 2 → 12 → 3) and walk the mechanism step by step; then the term ('isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain'), then the book's definition, then one line on where the learner meets it in real life. The example is the one Section 1 chose for the item (its place, actors, goods, numbers), economically correct and at the learner's level. The numbers are said the way a teacher tells what happened ('pehle aapke paas 500 rupaye the, kiraane ke 100 diye, ab 400 bache'), never as a state report (S2-09). The term is not named before the example by any teaching beat of the same concept either (a sister part may not explain 'the UPI route' before the ₹100 kirana payment runs; a hook or a question to the student may ask about it): BIE's code sends such a script back.
[S2-09] Complete teacher sentences (Navin's verdict on Money v1, 29 October 2026: 'teacher ki naration uske sentence aise poore ho ki banawati na lage aur cheejen samjhane ki process us par depend hai to unka complete tarike se istemal hona jaruri hai'): the narration tells what happened in full, natural sentences; a story's numbers are said conversationally ('pehle aapke paas 500 rupaye the, kiraane ke 100 diye, ab 400 bache'), never as a ledger's state report ('cash ₹500 से ₹400 हुआ', 'savings ₹0 से ₹500 हुईं'). BIE's code sends such a beat back.
[S2-10] Outside facts carry their dated source (the Money lesson resume -d, 29 October 2026, v10: operational descriptions of UPI, NEFT, RTGS and IMPS added real Indian banking knowledge beyond the book without a dated source): for a competitive-exam learner (level upsc_pcs), a teaching beat whose basis is outside the book, or mixed and naming an institution or system that none of its book lines names, carries its source with its year in `source` ('RBI, NEFT FAQ, 2023'); a story, example, hook, analogy or question needs none; a beat whose facts the book line says has basis 'book'. BIE's code sends such a beat back; the review page lists the outside beats with their sources.
[W-01] The narration never points at the book: no 'book के अनुसार', 'किताब कहती है', 'book says', 'page पर', 'textbook', 'NCERT' or any wording of that family (the list in this file, 'wording'). BIE teaches as a teacher: it says the fact itself. Navin accepts the copyright position (26 October 2026).

BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the result first (what it makes). 2) inputs and the place. 3) each step with its cause and its condition. 4) what breaks when a step fails. 5) the whole run once more at speed. 6) recap as a flow.
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the whole in context. 2) zoom into each part in a fixed path (outside to inside). 3) function of each part tied to its shape. 4) how the parts work together. 5) labelled recap.
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the overview tree first: the basis of division and every member named. 2) every member in the same slots: layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence. 3) the members compared side by side, the most confused pair named directly. 4) a memory trick for the family.
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what is common. 2) criteria one at a time, both sides together. 3) the reason behind each difference. 4) the most confused pair named directly. 5) difference table as recap.
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the period and its atmosphere. 2) events in order with their causes. 3) the people and their choices. 4) the turning point. 5) what changed after. 6) timeline recap.
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the effect students can see. 2) the cause. 3) each link of the chain with its mechanism. 4) the evidence. 5) the exception or limit. 6) the chain as recap.
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the fact in one line. 2) the number shown to scale against something familiar. 3) where it comes from (book or outside, dated). 4) what it changes or proves. 5) a formula built term by term when there is one.
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what the figure is and why it is here. 2) a reading path across it (labels in order). 3) the one thing to remember from it. 4) link back to the text it explains.
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) a concrete example first. 2) the book's definition word by word. 3) a non-example that tests the boundary. 4) where the term is used next in the chapter.

How BIE talks to you: every request is a task card (JSON) followed by its source. The card names the unit, its parts with their content type and required questions, the ids of the rules above that apply, the output, the ids you must cover and the context. The card is BIE's instruction; the source is the material.
For a write_script card:
- card.parts are this video's parts: each has item ids, one content type and the questions it must answer. The source gives every item's
  full content and its teacher questions with ids ("p003-i4#q2") and answers from BIE's chapter map; teach from them.
- card.coverage.must_cover lists every item this video must teach: each must be in covers_item_ids of a beat that really explains it.

  hook, analogy, where prerequisites are taught) with a reason each, what is uncertain.
- title: the video title in the learner language.
- parts: one entry per card part, with the universal frame of that part (S3-01), each in one or two lines of clear English for BIE:

Level profile: UPSC / State PCS (level_profiles.json; learners: UPSC and State PCS aspirants, often from arts backgrounds, who need understanding more than technical vocabulary).
- Terms: fewer technical terms: only the ones the exam asks, each opened with its plain meaning and an everyday image; a term the exam never asks is explained in words, not named.
- Why: 2 step(s); a two-step why from a need the learner can feel, then its link to daily life, health or governance.
- Where found: the main places, each linked to something the learner already knows (a disease, a food, a news item).
- Exam beats: the PYQ pattern: how this fact has been asked (statement combinations, 'which is correct', odd one out) and the wording that traps.
- Links: daily life, health, the news and earlier chapters of the same paper.

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-29.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- Open with a question on something visible (every new topic and every new family member): Skin aur stomach, kidney ke upar ek outer layer hai ki nahi? Yeh kis se bani hai? — phir naam: epithelial tissue.
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Contrast with the neighbour (members of one family, and what the exam confuses): Simple epithelium ka kaam protection nahi, woh compound ka hai. Zyada layers = pathogen andar nahi aata.
- Ask and repeat the key word (the one word the learner must keep): Irregular walls. Kaisi? Irregular.
- Exam memory beats by level (after the understanding, by the level profile): Yaad rakhna: brush border PCT mein. Doosre naam: pavement, tessellated. M2B = muscle to bone = tendon, B2B = bone to bone = ligament.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Teacher: absorptive surface yaani jahan cheezein andar li jaati hain, jaise aant khane ke poshak tatva sokhti hai; secretive yaani jahan cells kuch bana kar bahar chhodte hain, jaise glands enzyme ya juice. Aur epithelium wahan kyon? Kyunki ek patli, lagi hui parat hi cheezon ko paar jaane de sakti hai aur bana kar chhod sakti hai.
- Apply it in the real world first, then name it (Navin's sugar shop) (every economics concept (a definition, a cause-and-effect chain, a process): the example runs before the term is named): Ek kirana shop mein chini ke 3 packet hain, ₹50 ka ek. Kal 2 khareedar aaye the, aaj 12 aa gaye; sab ko chini chahiye par packet 3 hi hain. Dukandar daam ₹65 kar deta hai; ab sirf 3 log kharid paate hain, baaki 9 khaali haath. Zyada log, utna hi maal, isliye daam upar. Isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain. Phir book ki definition. Phir: yahi aap Diwali se pehle sabzi mandi mein dekhte hain.

Video v16: PYQ अभ्यास: blockchain, RTGS–NEFT और BHIM
Goal: Learner supplied questions के हर statement और option का कारण सहित निर्णय करेगा; blockchain applications और permission, settlement–charges–hours तथा BHIM interoperability और authentication की traps अलग पहचान सकेगा।
Opening hook: किसी statement का पहला हिस्सा सही हो, लेकिन आखिरी शब्द गलत हो—क्या आप उसे फिर भी सही चुनेंगे?
Story or analogy: हर supplied PYQ में पहले learner का निर्णय, फिर statement को छोटे claims में तोड़कर mechanism से जाँच होगी। Blockchain का ledger structure और applications जोड़ेंगे; technology को cryptocurrency तक सीमित नहीं करेंगे। Pre'25 wording में charge direction और hours, तथा BHIM में authentication factors और transaction steps अलग जाँचेंगे।
Planned minutes: 6
Narration time (S2-01): 4.8-6.5 minutes, about 624-845 spoken words (BIE counts 130 words a minute)
Prerequisites already taught in the prerequisite video (remind of one in at most 2 beats): Purchases, prices, debts and payments due later; Bank balances, deposits, loans and interest; Denominations, monetary arithmetic, percentages and minimum–maximum limits; Purchasing power, inflation, scarcity and liquidity; Central bank, commercial bank, government treasury and bank-to-bank settlement; Foreign currencies, exchange rates, reserves and demand–supply changes; Chronological reading: BCE/CE, centuries, dynasties and law versus implementation dates; Digital instructions, identity authentication, ledgers and payment interfaces
Open every book line (S2-07): a question about something the learner can see, then the name; every term opened: its plain meaning with 'yaani' and one everyday image (the word root where it helps); the why, starting from a need or a problem, one link at a time; an example or the place, by a zoom from the organ or the thing the learner knows; the consequence: what follows, and the link to the previous or the next idea; the contrast: what it is not, and what the exam confuses it with; the memory beat by level: the exam's 'yaad rakhna', the other names, the trick.

p019-i21 | 19 | paragraph | structure | 1. It is a public ledger that everyone can inspect, but which no single user controls.
  p019-i21#q1 | what | What is a ledger in this context? → It is a record book maintained electronically. In a public blockchain, participating computers maintain a shared history rather than leaving the authoritative record under one user's unilateral control. | outside
  p019-i21#q2 | where | Where are the records and control located? → Copies are maintained across participating network computers. Updates are accepted through the network's validation and agreement rules, rather than merely because one user edits a local copy. | outside
  p019-i21#q3 | how | How can inspection be open while editing is constrained? → Reading an entry gives information, not authority. A participant proposing a change must satisfy network rules; changing a private copy does not by itself change the shared accepted history. | outside
  p019-i21#q4 | why | Why use the image of several matching account books? → It separates access from control: many people may see the record, but one person's overwritten page is not automatically accepted by everyone else. | outside

  term | permission | yaani किसी मालिक से पहले मंजूरी लेना | image: खुले औजार से ऐप बनाना और किसी बंद दफ्तर में प्रवेश की मंजूरी अलग बातें हैं।

  example or place | Hypothetical onion delivery application, not a claim about an operating mandi system.

  p019-i24#q1 | how | How does a transfer move from the customer to completed interbank settlement? → The sender authorises a payment; the sending bank checks and submits it. In RTGS, an accepted payment settles individually through the banks' settlement accounts. In NEFT, instructions enter a batch and participating banks settle the resulting net obligations for that batch. The beneficiary bank then handles credit under the applicable system rules. | outside
  p019-i24#q2 | when | When does each system settle? → RTGS settles individual accepted instructions in real time, subject to system checks and available funds. NEFT settlement follows its half-hourly batch cycles rather than an individual gross settlement for each instruction. | outside

  p019-i24#q4 | how | How is interbank settlement different from an app notification? → Settlement completes obligations between participating banks. beats.say: आधा statement सही हो, तो पूरा चुनोगे?
मंडी का हिसाब कई लोगों के पास हो, तो क्या एक का बदलाव सबका हिसाब बदल देगा? Public blockchain का ledger ऐसा साझा electronic हिसाब है।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical mandi → shared electronic ledger

beats.say: Entry के पीछे participating computers पर copies हैं। बदलाव के लिए network के validation और agreement rules पूरे होने चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Entry → network copies → validation rules

beats.say: साझा rules एक user को अकेले history बदलने से रोकते हैं। देख सकना, बदलने का अधिकार नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Public inspection ≠ unilateral editing

beats.say: Entry पहले proposal है; checks के बाद accepted history बनती है। अपनी copy बदलना, network बदलना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Proposal → checks → accepted shared history

beats.say: हिसाब साझा है; control अकेले का नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Ledger | network copies | rule-based acceptance

beats.say: क्या इसमें प्याज की delivery लिख सकते हैं? Hypothetical मंडी में recorded quantity 0 से 10 sacks करनी है।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical delivery record: 0 → 10 sacks

beats.on_screen: Seller → authorised proposal: 10 sacks

beats.on_screen: Check → agreement → accepted 10 | Blockchain ≠ cryptocurrency only

beats.on_screen: Submit → validate → agree → share | Open development ≠ unrestricted conduct

beats.say: Delivery record भी checks से जुड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Goods report → checks → shared record

beats.say: ₹2,00,000 का stock खरीदने पर क्या होगा? Successful payment में buyer ₹5,00,000 से ₹3,00,000 और supplier ₹1,00,000 से ₹3,00,000 पर आएगा।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical stock payment ₹2,00,000 | Buyer ₹5,00,000 → ₹3,00,000 | Supplier ₹1,00,000 → ₹3,00,000

beats.say: Buyer bank A से authorise करता है; bank instruction जाँचता है। Supplier bank B में है; इसी दौर में दूसरा customer B से A को ₹50,000 भेजता है।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical customer instructions: A → B ₹2,00,000 | B → A ₹50,000

beats.say: पहले तरीके में payments पूरी रकम पर अलग settle होते हैं। दूसरे में batch का bank-level हिसाब ₹2,00,000 − ₹50,000 = ₹1,50,000 है; customers को पूरी रकम मिलती है। पहला RTGS, Real Time Gross Settlement है; दूसरा NEFT, National Electronic Funds Transfer है।
beats.on_screen: Alternative A: separate full-value obligations ₹2,00,000 and ₹50,000 → RTGS | Alternative B: ₹2,00,000 − ₹50,000 = ₹1,50,000 from A to B → NEFT | Customer amounts unchanged

beats.on_screen: Checks + funds required | Notification ≠ interbank settlement

beats.on_screen: Authorise → check → settle → credit | Customer notification is distinct

beats.say: Gross पूरा अलग; net बाकी रकम है।
beats.on_screen: Gross: full individual obligations | Net: offset bank obligations | No new customer money

beats.say: Supplier को दोनों तरीकों से पैसा मिलता है; फर्क कहाँ है? Settlement यानी भुगतान के पीछे बैंकों का आपसी हिसाब पूरा होना।
beats.on_screen: RTGS and NEFT: bank transfers | Compare settlement, inward charges and hours

beats.say: RTGS हर payment real time में अलग settle करता है; NEFT half-hourly batches में। Inward यानी खाते में पैसा आना: दोनों में receiving customer के लिए free है; दोनों 24×7 हैं।
beats.on_screen: RTGS: individual real time | NEFT: half-hourly batches | Both: inward free, 24×7

beats.on_screen: Sending ≠ receiving | Availability ≠ settlement mode

beats.on_screen: Comparison table: settlement differs | inward receipts free in both | both 24×7

problems.problem: The RTGS alternative settles both ₹2,00,000 and ₹50,000 separately. A ₹50,000 customer payment is below RTGS's ₹2 lakh minimum, so this is not a valid comparison of the same instructions under both systems.
problems.fix: Use eligible amounts in both directions, for example ₹3,00,000 and ₹2,00,000, and calculate the ₹1,00,000 net obligation. Update the opening balances consistently and cite a dated RBI source for the minimum. Replace the existing arithmetic rather than adding another example.

problems.problem: The first teaching beat names public blockchain before the prescribed 10-sack example runs. Even within that example, b9 names the application before b10 demonstrates the attempted replacement with 20 sacks.
problems.fix: Open with the seller recording 10 sacks, acceptance through checks, and the rejected attempt to replace 10 with 20. Then name blockchain and explain its ledger structure. Merge b5–b6 and b12 recap material to pay for the reordered explanation.

problems.problem: The numerical stories are stated as intended or predicted balance transitions rather than narrated events. In particular, 'recorded quantity 0 से 10 sacks करनी है' does not tell what actually happened.
problems.fix: Narrate the hypothetical events: the seller delivered ten sacks and submitted the record; the buyer paid the amount and the supplier received it. State starting balances and resulting balances as part of those events, replacing the existing transition wording.

problems.fix: Briefly describe the three PYQ mechanisms, the public-network and exam-year qualifications, and the rationale for the numerical examples.

beats.source: NIST, Blockchain Technology Overview, NISTIR 8202, 2018; UPSC, Civil Services Preliminary Examination, General Studies Paper I, 2020

beats.say: ₹3,00,000 का stock खरीदा, तो क्या हुआ? Buyer के पास ₹5,00,000 थे; भुगतान के बाद ₹2,00,000 बचे। Supplier के पास ₹1,00,000 थे; रकम मिलने पर ₹4,00,000 हुए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical completed purchase: ₹3,00,000 | Buyer ₹5,00,000 → ₹2,00,000 | Supplier ₹1,00,000 → ₹4,00,000

beats.say: Buyer ने bank A से payment authorise किया; bank ने जाँचा। Supplier bank B में था; उसी दौर में दूसरे customer ने B से A को ₹2,00,000 भेजे।
beats.on_screen: A → B: ₹3,00,000 | B → A: ₹2,00,000 | Compare alternative settlement methods
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: पहले तरीके में दोनों पूरी रकम अलग settle हुईं। दूसरे में batch का net ₹1,00,000 A से B गया; customers को पूरी रकम मिली। पहला RTGS, Real Time Gross Settlement; दूसरा NEFT, National Electronic Funds Transfer कहलाता है। RTGS का minimum ₹2,00,000 है।
beats.on_screen: RTGS: ₹3,00,000 and ₹2,00,000 separately | Minimum ₹2,00,000 | NEFT batch: ₹3,00,000 − ₹2,00,000 = ₹1,00,000 A → B | Full customer amounts
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: Checks या funds अधूरे हों, तो settlement अटक सकता है। App notification का मतलब बैंकों का हिसाब पूरा होना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Checks + funds required | Notification ≠ interbank settlement
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: Supplier payment में authorisation, checks, bank settlement और beneficiary credit आते हैं; notification अलग पहचानो।
beats.on_screen: Authorise → check → settle → credit | Notification is distinct
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: Gross में पूरा payment अलग; net में आपसी बाकी रकम settle होती है।
beats.on_screen: Gross: full individual obligations | Net: offset bank obligations
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: Supplier को दोनों तरीकों से पैसा मिलता है; फर्क कहाँ है? Settlement यानी भुगतान के पीछे बैंकों का आपसी हिसाब पूरा होना।
beats.on_screen: Compare settlement, inward charges and operating hours
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: RTGS हर payment real time में अलग settle करता है; NEFT half-hourly batches में। Inward यानी खाते में पैसा आना: दोनों में receiving customer के लिए free है; दोनों 24×7 हैं।
beats.on_screen: RTGS: individual real time | NEFT: half-hourly batches | Both: inward free, 24×7
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: NEFT में batch का इंतजार है; RTGS में नहीं। RBI ने NEFT को 16 December 2019 और RTGS को 14 December 2020 से round-the-clock किया, दोनों 2025 से पहले।
beats.on_screen: NEFT: 16 December 2019 | RTGS: 14 December 2020 → Both precede 2025
beats.source: RBI, Availability of NEFT System on 24x7 Basis, 2019; RBI, RTGS System—Availability on 24x7 Basis, 2020

beats.say: भेजने का charge, पाने का charge नहीं है। 24×7 खुलना भी real-time settlement नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Sending ≠ receiving | Availability ≠ settlement mode
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: Settlement अलग है; दोनों inward-free और 24×7 हैं।
beats.on_screen: Settlement differs | Inward receipts free in both | Both 24×7
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: 2025 में I सही; instantaneous real-time model है, zero-delay guarantee नहीं। II का inward charge और III के restricted days गलत हैं।
beats.on_screen: I ✓ II ✗ III ✗
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: a सही है: I real-time और batch का फर्क बताता है। b गलत है क्योंकि II पाने वाले पर charge लगाता है।
beats.on_screen: (a) I only ✓ | (b) I and II ✗
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: c और d में गलत III है: दोनों 24×7 हैं। d सही I भी छोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: (c) I and III ✗ | (d) III only ✗
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: अलग app वाले merchant को ₹500 कैसे मिले? तुम्हारे खाते में ₹2,000 थे; किराने के ₹500 दिए, ₹1,500 बचे। Merchant के ₹3,000 थे; मिलने पर ₹3,500 हुए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical completed grocery payment: ₹500 | Shopper ₹2,000 → ₹1,500 | Merchant ₹3,000 → ₹3,500

beats.say: तुमने merchant का linked account चुना, नाम और ₹500 जाँचे। Registered device पर UPI PIN डालकर payment authorise किया।
beats.on_screen: Verify payee and ₹500 → authorise on registered device with UPI PIN
beats.source: NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: Network और banks ने processing पूरी की, तभी रकम पहुँची। यह BHIM से UPI transfer है; Unified Payments Interface eligible bank accounts जोड़ता है, same app जरूरी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: BHIM → UPI → linked accounts | Existing ₹500 transferred, not created
beats.source: NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016; NPCI, BHIM launch announcement, 2016

beats.say: Amount भरना काफी नहीं; authorisation या processing अधूरी हो, तो payment completed मत मानो।
beats.on_screen: Amount entered ≠ successful payment
beats.source: NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: खरीद में payee जाँचो, authorise करो, फिर successful status और receipt confirm करो।
beats.on_screen: Verify → authorise → process → confirm
beats.source: NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: BHIM दरवाजा है, UPI रास्ता; पैसा जुड़े accounts में जाता है।
beats.on_screen: App ≠ network ≠ account
beats.source: NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016; NPCI, BHIM launch announcement, 2016

beats.say: Card लगाना और PIN डालना क्या अलग सबूत हैं? Authentication factors यानी पहचान के अलग तरह के सबूत; card और BHIM दोनों में possession और knowledge हैं।
beats.on_screen: Authentication evidence: possession + knowledge
beats.source: RBI, Report of the Working Group on Securing Card Present Transactions, 2011; NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: Card में possession का सबूत card है; BHIM में registered mobile/device linkage। Knowledge दोनों में secret PIN की है।
beats.on_screen: Card + card PIN | Registered device linkage + UPI PIN
beats.source: RBI, Report of the Working Group on Securing Card Present Transactions, 2011; NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: Bank को proof चाहिए, clicks नहीं। चाबी और secret code अलग proof हैं; बार-बार चाबी घुमाना नए factors नहीं बनाता।
beats.on_screen: Possession + knowledge | Repeated actions ≠ new factors
beats.source: RBI, Report of the Working Group on Securing Card Present Transactions, 2011; NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: Payee, amount और confirmation screens actions हैं, independent factors नहीं। Chip-pin card को four-factor कहना गलत है।
beats.on_screen: Transaction steps ≠ authentication factors | Four-factor premise ✗
beats.source: RBI, Report of the Working Group on Securing Card Present Transactions, 2011; NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: Possession का सबूत अलग है; PIN knowledge दोनों में है।
beats.on_screen: Card versus registered device linkage | PIN knowledge shared
beats.source: RBI, Report of the Working Group on Securing Card Present Transactions, 2011; NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: 2018 में 1 सही, 2 गलत। BHIM की two-factor बात card का four-factor दावा सही नहीं बनाती; screens गिनना factors गिनना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: 1 ✓ 2 ✗ | Evaluate both halves
beats.source: RBI, Report of the Working Group on Securing Card Present Transactions, 2011; NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: a सही: UPI-enabled accounts तक पहुँच है। b गलत: false 2 चुनता और सही 1 छोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: (a) 1 only ✓ | (b) 2 only ✗
beats.source: NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016; RBI, Report of the Working Group on Securing Card Present Transactions, 2011

beats.say: c गलत 2 जोड़ता है। d भी गलत: interoperability वाला सही 1 हटा देता है।
beats.on_screen: (c) Both ✗ | (d) Neither ✗
beats.source: RBI, Report of the Working Group on Securing Card Present Transactions, 2011; NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: Access, hours और screens से control, settlement और factors मत तय करो।
beats.on_screen: Access ≠ control | Hours ≠ settlement | Steps ≠ factors
beats.source: NIST, Blockchain Technology Overview, NISTIR 8202, 2018; RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023; NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

frame.atmosphere: A supplier checking receipt of a customer's bank payment.

frame.process: Trace one hypothetical stock payment under two alternative settlement methods.

frame.atmosphere: A shop owner paying a supplier at another bank.

beats.say: आधा statement सही हो, तो पूरा चुनोगे?
Seller ने 10 प्याज के sacks पहुँचाए; साझा हिसाब कैसे बनेगा? पहले कोई entry नहीं थी; अब उसने 10 sacks की entry भेजी।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical mandi: seller delivers 10 sacks and submits an entry.

beats.say: Seller ने authorised record भेजा; application के rules के मुताबिक buyer की confirmation भी जोड़ी। Participating computers ने इसे जाँचा।
beats.on_screen: Authorised delivery report → participating validators
beats.source: NIST, Blockchain Technology Overview, NISTIR 8202, 2018

beats.say: Authorisation और format सही मिले; network के agreement rules पूरे हुए। तभी 10 sacks की entry साझा accepted history में जुड़ी।
beats.on_screen: Check authorisation and format → agreement → accept 10 sacks
beats.source: NIST, Blockchain Technology Overview, NISTIR 8202, 2018

beats.say: Viewer ने 10 मिटाकर 20 लिखा, लेकिन unsupported बदलाव accepted नहीं हुआ। यह blockchain delivery application है; validation असल delivery का proof नहीं, उसके लिए भरोसेमंद reporting चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Local overwrite: 10 → 20 rejected | Blockchain application: delivery records
beats.source: NIST, Blockchain Technology Overview, NISTIR 8202, 2018

beats.say: Report से checks, फिर agreement से entry बनी। Permissionless features पर development को central owner की मंजूरी नहीं चाहिए; कानून और private-network access rules फिर भी लागू हैं।
beats.on_screen: Report → checks → agreement → entry | Open development ≠ unrestricted access or conduct
beats.source: NIST, Blockchain Technology Overview, NISTIR 8202, 2018; World Economic Forum, Blockchain Beyond the Hype, 2018

beats.say: Checks से जुड़ा delivery record cryptocurrency का record नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Delivery report → validation → shared record | Not cryptocurrency-only
beats.source: NIST, Blockchain Technology Overview, NISTIR 8202, 2018

beats.say: अब यह साझा हिसाब कहाँ रहता है? Public blockchain का ledger यानी electronic हिसाब, जैसे कई लोगों के पास matching account books।
beats.on_screen: Public blockchain ledger: shared electronic record
beats.source: NIST, Blockchain Technology Overview, NISTIR 8202, 2018

beats.say: Entry की copies participating computers पर रहती हैं; accepted history network के validation और agreement rules से बनती है।
beats.on_screen: Entry → network copies → validation and agreement
beats.source: NIST, Blockchain Technology Overview, NISTIR 8202, 2018

beats.say: Shared rules अकेले user को accepted history बदलने नहीं देते। Public inspection यानी देख सकना, editing का अधिकार नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Inspection ≠ unilateral editing authority
beats.source: NIST, Blockchain Technology Overview, NISTIR 8202, 2018

beats.say: Proposal पर checks होते हैं; agreement से shared history बदलती है। अपनी copy बदलने से बाकी network नहीं बदलता।
beats.on_screen: Proposal → checks → agreement → accepted history
beats.source: NIST, Blockchain Technology Overview, NISTIR 8202, 2018

beats.say: Ledger साझा है; control अकेले का नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Ledger | distributed copies | shared acceptance rules
beats.source: NIST, Blockchain Technology Overview, NISTIR 8202, 2018

beats.say: 2020 में public permissionless context में 1 और 3 सही; 2 का ‘cryptocurrency only’ गलत। तुम्हारा combination क्या होगा?
beats.on_screen: 1 ✓ 2 ✗ 3 ✓ | Public, permissionless context
beats.source: NIST, Blockchain Technology Overview, NISTIR 8202, 2018; UPSC, Civil Services Preliminary Examination, General Studies Paper I, 2020

beats.say: a गलत है क्योंकि सही statement 3 छूटता है। b भी गलत है क्योंकि गलत 2 जुड़ता है और सही 3 छूटता है।
beats.on_screen: a: omits 3 ✗ | b: includes 2, omits 3 ✗
beats.source: NIST, Blockchain Technology Overview, NISTIR 8202, 2018; UPSC, Civil Services Preliminary Examination, General Studies Paper I, 2020

beats.on_screen: c: 2 only ✗ | d: 1 and 3 only ✓

beats.say: ₹3,00,000 का stock खरीदा, तो क्या हुआ? Buyer के ₹5,00,000 में ₹2,00,000 बचे। Supplier के पास ₹1,00,000 थे; payment मिलने पर ₹4,00,000 हुए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical completed purchase: ₹3,00,000 | Buyer ₹5,00,000 → ₹2,00,000 | Supplier ₹1,00,000 → ₹4,00,000

beats.say: Buyer ने bank A से payment authorise किया; bank ने जाँचा। Supplier bank B में था; उसी दौर में दूसरे customer ने B से A को ₹2,00,000 भेजे।
beats.on_screen: A → B: ₹3,00,000 | B → A: ₹2,00,000 | Compare alternative settlement methods
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: पहले तरीके में पूरी रकम अलग-अलग settle हुई। दूसरे में batch का net ₹1,00,000 A से B गया; customers को पूरी रकम मिली। पहला RTGS, Real Time Gross Settlement; दूसरा NEFT, National Electronic Funds Transfer है। RTGS का minimum ₹2,00,000 है।
beats.on_screen: RTGS: ₹3,00,000 and ₹2,00,000 separately | Minimum ₹2,00,000 | NEFT batch: ₹3,00,000 − ₹2,00,000 = ₹1,00,000 A → B | Full customer amounts
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: Checks या funds अधूरे हों, तो settlement अटक सकता है। App notification का मतलब बैंकों का हिसाब पूरा होना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Checks + funds required | Notification ≠ interbank settlement
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: Supplier payment में authorisation, checks, bank settlement और beneficiary credit आते हैं; notification अलग पहचानो।
beats.on_screen: Authorise → check → settle → credit | Notification is distinct
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: Gross में पूरा payment अलग; net में आपसी बाकी रकम settle होती है।
beats.on_screen: Gross: full individual obligations | Net: offset bank obligations
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: Supplier को दोनों तरीकों से पैसा मिलता है; फर्क कहाँ है? Settlement यानी भुगतान के पीछे बैंकों का आपसी हिसाब पूरा होना।
beats.on_screen: Compare settlement, inward charges and operating hours
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: RTGS हर payment real time में अलग settle करता है; NEFT half-hourly batches में। Inward यानी खाते में पैसा आना: दोनों में receiving customer के लिए free है; दोनों 24×7 हैं।
beats.on_screen: RTGS: individual real time | NEFT: half-hourly batches | Both: inward free, 24×7
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: NEFT में batch का इंतजार है; RTGS में नहीं। RBI ने NEFT को 16 December 2019 और RTGS को 14 December 2020 से round-the-clock किया, दोनों 2025 से पहले।
beats.on_screen: NEFT: 16 December 2019 | RTGS: 14 December 2020 → Both precede 2025
beats.source: RBI, Availability of NEFT System on 24x7 Basis, 2019; RBI, RTGS System—Availability on 24x7 Basis, 2020

beats.say: भेजने का charge, पाने का charge नहीं है। 24×7 खुलना भी real-time settlement नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Sending ≠ receiving | Availability ≠ settlement mode
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: Settlement अलग है; दोनों inward-free और 24×7 हैं।
beats.on_screen: Settlement differs | Inward receipts free in both | Both 24×7
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: 2025 में I सही; instantaneous real-time model है, zero-delay guarantee नहीं। II का inward charge और III के restricted days गलत हैं।
beats.on_screen: I ✓ II ✗ III ✗
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: a सही है: I real-time और batch का फर्क बताता है। b गलत है क्योंकि II पाने वाले पर charge लगाता है।
beats.on_screen: (a) I only ✓ | (b) I and II ✗
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: c और d में गलत III है: दोनों 24×7 हैं। d सही I भी छोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: (c) I and III ✗ | (d) III only ✗
beats.source: RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023

beats.say: अलग app वाले merchant को ₹500 कैसे मिले? तुम्हारे ₹2,000 में किराने के ₹500 देने पर ₹1,500 बचे। Merchant के ₹3,000 थे; payment मिलने पर ₹3,500 हुए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical completed grocery payment: ₹500 | Shopper ₹2,000 → ₹1,500 | Merchant ₹3,000 → ₹3,500

beats.say: तुमने merchant का linked account चुना, नाम और ₹500 जाँचे। Registered device पर UPI PIN डालकर payment authorise किया।
beats.on_screen: Verify payee and ₹500 → authorise on registered device with UPI PIN
beats.source: NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: Network और banks ने processing पूरी की, तभी रकम पहुँची। यह BHIM से UPI transfer है; Unified Payments Interface eligible bank accounts जोड़ता है, same app जरूरी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: BHIM → UPI → linked accounts | Existing ₹500 transferred, not created
beats.source: NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016; NPCI, BHIM launch announcement, 2016

beats.say: Amount भरना काफी नहीं; authorisation या processing अधूरी हो, तो payment completed मत मानो।
beats.on_screen: Amount entered ≠ successful payment
beats.source: NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: खरीद में payee जाँचो, authorise करो, फिर successful status और receipt confirm करो।
beats.on_screen: Verify → authorise → process → confirm
beats.source: NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: BHIM दरवाजा है, UPI रास्ता; पैसा जुड़े accounts में जाता है।
beats.on_screen: App ≠ network ≠ account
beats.source: NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016; NPCI, BHIM launch announcement, 2016

beats.say: Card लगाना और PIN डालना क्या अलग सबूत हैं? Authentication factors यानी पहचान के अलग तरह के सबूत; card और BHIM दोनों में possession और knowledge हैं।
beats.on_screen: Authentication evidence: possession + knowledge
beats.source: RBI, Report of the Working Group on Securing Card Present Transactions, 2011; NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: Card में possession का सबूत card है; BHIM में registered mobile/device linkage। Knowledge दोनों में secret PIN की है।
beats.on_screen: Card + card PIN | Registered device linkage + UPI PIN
beats.source: RBI, Report of the Working Group on Securing Card Present Transactions, 2011; NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: Bank को proof चाहिए, clicks नहीं। चाबी और secret code अलग proof हैं; बार-बार चाबी घुमाना नए factors नहीं बनाता।
beats.on_screen: Possession + knowledge | Repeated actions ≠ new factors
beats.source: RBI, Report of the Working Group on Securing Card Present Transactions, 2011; NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: Payee, amount और confirmation screens actions हैं, independent factors नहीं। Chip-pin card को four-factor कहना गलत है।
beats.on_screen: Transaction steps ≠ authentication factors | Four-factor premise ✗
beats.source: RBI, Report of the Working Group on Securing Card Present Transactions, 2011; NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: Possession का सबूत अलग है; PIN knowledge दोनों में है।
beats.on_screen: Card versus registered device linkage | PIN knowledge shared
beats.source: RBI, Report of the Working Group on Securing Card Present Transactions, 2011; NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: 2018 में 1 सही, 2 गलत। BHIM की two-factor बात card का four-factor दावा सही नहीं बनाती; screens गिनना factors गिनना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: 1 ✓ 2 ✗ | Evaluate both halves
beats.source: RBI, Report of the Working Group on Securing Card Present Transactions, 2011; NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: a सही: UPI-enabled accounts तक पहुँच है। b गलत: false 2 चुनता और सही 1 छोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: (a) 1 only ✓ | (b) 2 only ✗
beats.source: NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016; RBI, Report of the Working Group on Securing Card Present Transactions, 2011

beats.say: c गलत 2 जोड़ता है। d भी गलत: interoperability वाला सही 1 हटा देता है।
beats.on_screen: (c) Both ✗ | (d) Neither ✗
beats.source: RBI, Report of the Working Group on Securing Card Present Transactions, 2011; NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

beats.say: Access, hours और screens से control, settlement और factors मत तय करो।
beats.on_screen: Access ≠ control | Hours ≠ settlement | Steps ≠ factors
beats.source: NIST, Blockchain Technology Overview, NISTIR 8202, 2018; RBI, RTGS System FAQ and NEFT System FAQ, 2023; NPCI, UPI Procedural Guidelines, 2016

notes.about: This unit teaches three PYQ clusters through worked examples, mechanism-based statement checks and option elimination. It distinguishes blockchain access from control, payment availability from settlement, and authentication factors from procedural steps.
key_questions: Why can blockchain record deliveries without allowing unilateral changes?
How do RTGS and NEFT differ in settlement while sharing inward-charge and availability rules?
Why can BHIM reach other UPI users, and why are transaction screens not authentication factors?
